newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on institutional buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended sharply up on Friday on institutional buying at low levels, traders said.

The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,100 yuan ($373) per tonne, up 80 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,040. March rose 80 to 3,100, May 30 to 3,130, July 40 to 3,160, September 131 to 3,310 and November 64 to 3,290.
Combined volume rose to 15,100 tonnes from 14,000.
Traders said institutional buying triggered heavy follow-up speculative buying, resulting in today's sharp rises.
"Open interest of all contracts except January rose sharply, indicating that institutions built many long positions at low levels," one trader said.
"Successive sharp losses over the past few days have made big rebounds possible in the next few days," he added.
Analysts expect soybean to rise further on institutional support in the next few days.
